name: Thomas M Siebel
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, C3.ai (CEO until Sept 2025)
profile: Tom Siebel, an Oracle sales executive in the 1980s, founded CRM pioneer Siebel Systems in 1993 and sold it to Oracle for ~$5.8B in 2006. He founded enterprise-AI software firm C3.ai (originally C3 Energy, focused on smart-grid analytics), was CEO 2011-2025 and handed the CEO role to Stephen Ehikian in Sept 2025, remaining executive chairman.
interesting_fact: C3.ai began life in 2009 as C3 Energy, building analytics for utilities and the power grid -- a direct tie-in to an energy/data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: In 2005 his Thomas and Stacey Siebel Foundation started the Montana Meth Project, a graphic teen-prevention ad campaign; he testified about it to the U.S. Senate Finance Committee in Sept 2007, and Montana teen meth use reportedly fell 63% over four years.
notes: Stepped back from CEO role in 2025; still executive chairman. Siebel Energy Institute and Siebel Scholars are relevant to energy/data themes. Best route is via C3.ai PR.

name: Nikolaus Knauf
current_role: Shareholder and longtime member/former chair of the shareholders' committee, Knauf Group (Iphofen, Germany)
profile: Born 1936, the eldest son of Knauf co-founder Alfons Knauf. From 1969 he co-ran the family plasterboard/building-materials group with cousin Baldwin Knauf, overseeing technology while it expanded across Europe, Russia and the CIS; he left management in 2008 for the shareholders' committee. Knauf remains fully family-owned (~EUR 15B sales).
interesting_fact: Knauf was founded in 1932 by brothers Alfons and Karl Knauf as a gypsum works in Perl on the Moselle before moving to Iphofen in Lower Franconia, where the family's Knauf-Museum (opened 1983) shows casts of great relief artworks.
deep_cut_fact: Within the cousin duo running Knauf, Nikolaus handled the technical side while Baldwin took administration; he has also served as a CSU councillor in the small municipality of Markt Einersheim near Iphofen and on the Kitzingen district council.

public_contacts.value: Gebr. Knauf KG, Corporate Communications, Iphofen (press-release contact)

notes: Aged ~90, very private, no personal channels. Was honorary consul of Russia in Nuremberg until March 2022 (Knauf's Russia business was a sensitive topic after 2022) -- avoid. Route via Knauf corporate communications.

name: Woody Johnson
current_role: Chairman and co-owner, New York Jets; partner and director, Crystal Palace FC
profile: Robert Wood 'Woody' Johnson IV is a great-grandson of Johnson & Johnson co-founder Robert Wood Johnson I, and his wealth stems from the J&J family fortune. He bought the New York Jets in 2000 for $635M, helped build MetLife Stadium, served as U.S. Ambassador to the UK (2017-2021) and is back as Jets chairman.
interesting_fact: As ambassador he led the U.S. Embassy London's move to its new headquarters at Nine Elms.
deep_cut_fact: He has been a pioneer backer of women's and girls' flag football from youth to international level, and has held civic roles with the Wildlife Conservation Society and the Peregrine Fund (a raptor-conservation group).
notes: No source_of_wealth in input; identity confirmed via Wikidata Q3569866 (Jets owner). Founded the Lupus Research Alliance. Best route via Jets communications.

name: Jeff Rothschild
current_role: Private investor; Facebook founding infrastructure executive (retired 2015); vice chair, Vanderbilt University Board of Trust; director, Pure Storage (joined 2018)
profile: Rothschild co-founded storage-software company Veritas Software (1988; sold to Symantec for $13.5B in 2004) and online-gaming network Mpath Interactive (1995). He joined Facebook in 2005 as VP of infrastructure engineering, building out its backend systems, moved to an advisory role around 2010 and left in 2015; his fortune comes mainly from Facebook stock.
interesting_fact: When Facebook hired him in 2005 he was 50 years old, making him the company's oldest executive at the time.
deep_cut_fact: Before Facebook he co-founded Mpath Interactive in 1995, an early internet multiplayer-gaming/voice company that went public in 1999, and he is a co-inventor on several of its patents; he began his career as an engineer at Honeywell and Intel.
notes: Low public profile, no personal social channels found. Strong data-center/infra angle (ran Facebook infrastructure in its scale-up years, storage background). Possible routes: via Vanderbilt or Pure Storage board, but no published contact for him personally. Not related to the banking Rothschilds.

name: Jonathan Kwok
current_role: Director, Empire Group Holdings (Hong Kong property developer)
profile: Younger son of the late Walter Kwok, former chairman of Sun Hung Kai Properties. After Walter's death in 2018, Jonathan and brother Geoffrey inherited his SHKP stake and took over Empire Group Holdings, the developer Walter founded; Jonathan leads its real estate investment, project development and asset management.
interesting_fact: He was ranked the world's sixth-youngest billionaire in 2020; he studied at Cornell's School of Hotel Administration and worked at CSI Properties and CMB International Securities before Empire.
deep_cut_fact: The 'E' in Empire Group's logo was handwritten by his father Walter, and Jonathan and his brother completed the remaining letters in tribute.
notes: Avoid the family feud/kidnapping history of his father. General company inbox is the only published route.

name: Shlomo Eliahu
current_role: Controlling shareholder and director, Migdal Insurance & Financial Holdings (stepped down as chair in 2022); chairman, Eliahu Insurance
profile: Born in Baghdad in 1936, Eliahu emigrated to Israel at 14 and grew up in a transit camp and south Tel Aviv. He opened an insurance agency in 1955, founded Eliahu Insurance (the first company licensed to sell insurance after statehood), was a Knesset member 1977-1981, and in 2012 bought control of Migdal, Israel's leading insurer, where he remains controlling holder.
interesting_fact: He served in the Knesset (Dash/Democratic Movement, then his own Ahva faction) and chaired the Knesset's capital-markets subcommittee before quitting politics in 1981.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he worked as a messenger boy at Migdal -- the insurer he bought control of in 2012. His first agency (1955) ran from the corner of a motorcycle-repair garage in Tel Aviv's Shapira neighborhood, and he signed up clients by bicycle while also promoting entertainment shows.
notes: Aged ~90; no death reported. Hanan Melcer replaced him as Migdal chair (2022, Globes). Quote from honorary-fellow citation: 'The hardships forged me. Wealth never spoke to me.' No personal contact channel found; route via Migdal corporate.

name: Johan Johannson
profile: Fifth-generation heir to a trading business founded in 1866 by an earlier Johan Johannson from Askim. With his father Knut Hartvig Johannson he controls about 75% of NorgesGruppen (Kiwi, Meny, Spar, Joker; ~40% of Norway's grocery market). A BI business graduate, he joined the family firm in 1995, ran retail, property and new ventures, and succeeded his father as chairman in 2022.
interesting_fact: The family business began in 1866 as a coffee importer/wholesaler (known for the Ali Kaffe brand) before evolving into Norway's largest grocery group.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he spent 1991-1995 as a consultant at Andersen Consulting (now Accenture); his uncle Torbjorn Johannson recruited him in 1995 to be the day-to-day driving force of holding company Joh. Johannson. He is also a certified retail worker (butikkfagarbeider).
notes: Forbes bio is outdated: he is now chairman (father stepped down 2022). Family keeps a low profile. Press emails are named NorgesGruppen communications staff listed in its NTB press room.

name: Bhushan Dua
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, T-Series (Super Cassettes Industries Pvt Ltd), Mumbai/Noida
profile: Bhushan Kumar Dua (b. 1977, Delhi), son of T-Series founder Gulshan Kumar, took charge of the music label as a teenager in 1997 with his uncle Krishan Kumar. He built T-Series into India's largest music label and a major Bollywood producer (Aashiqui 2, Hindi Medium, Animal, Bhool Bhulaiyaa franchise), and its YouTube channel became one of the world's most-subscribed.
interesting_fact: He is credited as producer on 100+ films since Tum Bin (2001); T-Series' Hindi Medium won him the Filmfare Award for Best Film.
notes: Listed as Bhushan Dua; publicly known as Bhushan Kumar. T-Series site says to contact exclusively via its contact page. Avoid father's 1997 murder and past allegations/tax probe. No sourced deep-cut fact found beyond widely known film credits.

name: Jian Yao
current_role: Shareholder, Shenzhen Mindray Bio-Medical Electronics (no known operating role)
profile: Per Forbes, Jian Yao is the ex-wife of Xu Hang, co-founder of Shenzhen medical-device maker Mindray (founded 1991), and obtained a minority stake in Mindray in 2020 after their divorce; that stake is the source of her fortune. No public role or activities found.
interesting_fact: Mindray, set up in Shenzhen in 1991, is one of China's largest medical-device makers; co-founder Xu Hang worked at Shenzhen Anke High-Tech (1987-1991), where he met fellow co-founders Li Xiting and Cheng Minghe.
notes: Wealth comes from a divorce settlement; she is a private individual with no public profile, so independent verification beyond Forbes was not possible. Not a good outreach target; avoid any reference to the divorce.

name: He Yi
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO (since Dec 2025, with Richard Teng), Binance; head of YZi Labs (formerly Binance Labs)
profile: Yi He (born He Ying, 1986, rural Sichuan) co-founded crypto exchange Binance with Changpeng Zhao in 2017 after marketing roles at OKCoin and live-streaming firm Yixia. Long Binance's marketing and customer-service chief, she has run its venture arm Binance Labs (now YZi Labs, investing in Web3, AI and biotech) since 2022 and was named co-CEO on 3 Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: Her co-CEO appointment was announced on stage at Binance Blockchain Week in Dubai as the exchange neared 300 million users.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto she trained in counselling psychology, taught for two years at a private arts college in Lijiang, and hosted travel TV programmes (Travel Satellite TV, Beijing TV) in 2012-2014; at OKCoin she ran a Times Square billboard campaign.
notes: Based in Dubai (UAE). Highly visible on social media, but I could not verify her personal X handle from an official page, so it is not listed. Avoid Zhao's legal case and personal relationship. Route via Binance press/communications.
